thread:
inc-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT SEV2 — Elevated 5xx + timeouts affecting control-plane routes (/auth, /org-lookup, /config). Started ~10:02 UTC. Paging @amy (sre) @jay (eng-runtime) @zack (eng-oncall)

amy (sre): ack. I'm on it. Can everyone drop any ongoing deploys please?

jay (eng-runtime): seeing a sharp spike in error rate from gateway: 502/504s and some 500s. Error pattern points at auth-org-lookup calls timing out (latency to auth-db up ~700ms).

devon (platform): rolling CPU on auth-deployment made no difference. Traffic graph: concentrated on hosted-api region-us-west-2, but also cross-region fanout.

sam (product): CS reporting customers seeing generation failures with 502/timeout. Need ETA for mitigation to give customers. Maria, can you triage customer impact?

maria (cs): on it — customers affected: ~12 tenants, mostly heavy concurrent sessions (streaming). Opening a support doc and sending a status update once we have a mitigation.

ajay (typo) — ignore

jay (eng-runtime): quick logs snapshot:
```
2026-03-15T10:03:15Z gateway: upstream error 502 auth-proxy
2026-03-15T10:03:16Z auth-org-lookup: WARNING call timeout after 500ms for tenant=acme
2026-03-15T10:03:16Z config-service: GET /v1/route failed -> 504
```

amy (sre): hypothesis: auth token validation path is stalling on org-lookup which has a bad memcache layer after the last deploy. Could be transient cache eviction / DB connection saturation.

zack (eng-oncall): I can flip a quick circuit-breaker to short-circuit org-lookup for non-critical callers (internal admin etc). Would reduce pressure. Thoughts?

devon (platform): ++ circuit-breaker for org-lookup read path. Also recommend enabling auth-cached-fallback: serve cached org metadata for 30s when org-lookup times out. We have that code path but it's currently off for some tenants.

jay (eng-runtime): I can enable fallback globally for hosted nodes and toggle region by region. Doing a controlled enable in us-west-2 now (will take ~60s to roll).

amy (sre): while Jay rolls, I'm going to scale up auth-org-lookup replicas by +2 and temporarily increase DB connection pool. Keep an eye on RPS.

ops-bot: deploybot: starting config toggle: `auth.cached_fallback = true` in us-west-2 (canary 10%).

jay (eng-runtime): canary toggled to 10% @10:06 UTC. Monitoring error rate.

amy (sre): early signals: 10% canary shows 5xx drop ~40% for those hosts. Gateway 5xx overall still ~12% above baseline.

maria (cs): sending first customer note: "We're aware of elevated errors affecting API responses. Engineers are actively mitigating. Next update in 15m."

devon (platform): While we wait, let's add a throttling rule: limit bursty admin/ingest calls to reduce backend fanout. Pushing a temporary rate-limit rule at edge.

zack (eng-oncall): applied rate-limit rule for `/batch/*` and admin endpoints at CDN edge. Should prevent some noise from noisy tenants.

jay (eng-runtime): rolling cached_fallback to 60% now. Observability: auth latency p95 dropping from 720ms -> 180ms on fallbacks.

amy (sre): scaling and fallback combined -> gateway 5xxs dropping from peak ~18% -> ~4% within 8 minutes. This is promising.

sam (product): good. Can we estimate user-visible impacted percentage and whether to declare degraded?

maria (cs): based on logs and customer reports, ~8% of requests were returning 5xx earlier; now reduced to ~1.2%. Still some sessions affected (>95th percentile users saw interruptions).

amy (sre): I'll keep this as SEV2 degraded for now. Next steps: 1) keep cached_fallback on until root cause fixed, 2) run a controlled rollback of the last memcache/config deploy to org-lookup, 3) investigate memcache eviction pattern and DB connection exhaustion.

devon (platform): starting rollback of last org-lookup deploy to previous image (rolling across regions). Estimated 10 minutes.

ops-bot: deploybot: rollback initiated for `org-lookup-service` to image `org-lookup:v2026.03.10` by devon.

jay (eng-runtime): rollback in progress. I'll continue the cached_fallback toggle as needed.

amy (sre): monitoring: after rollback begins, errors continue to fall. We'll keep connection pool increases until memcache patch deployed.

maria (cs): preparing customer follow-up explaining: temporary cached fallback enabled; root cause under investigation; no data loss.

zack (eng-oncall): PS: we should add a targeted synthetic test hitting org-lookup to catch regressions. I'll add to runbook.

sam (product): good. Are there any dependents we need to notify internally? Eng-runtime, eng-platform, security (if memcache creds?), and support already looped.

devon (platform): no evidence of credential leak. This looks like resource pressure + config change. Security on standby.

amy (sre): handing off to night oncall: @zack will own remaining validation and postmortem follow-up. I'll stay available for escalation for the next hour.

zack (eng-oncall): acked, taking over at 10:25 UTC. Milestones for handoff: ensure cached_fallback remains enabled for 30m after stabilization, confirm rollback fully rolled in all regions, gather logs for postmortem (memcache eviction trace, DB metrics).

maria (cs): customer update queued. Will send after stabilization confirmation.

inc-bot: NOTE: Handoff recorded. Incident channel updated. SEV2 -> in mitigation -> assigned to zack (eng-oncall).

amy (sre): thanks team. Follow-up actions recorded: CH1: postmortem, CH2: guardrail to prevent disabling cached_fallback accidentally, CH3: add synthetic org-lookup tests and better memcache alerts.

zack (eng-oncall): closing the live debugging thread — moving to `#postmortems` for write-up when we have logs. If anything regresses ping me.
